```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a sector
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose esef section names the Silver layer of
# the module and whose financialreport section names the combined tables the
# benchmark is read from. A chunk runs with the directory of this template
# as its working directory, which is inside the installed package, so the
# path is taken from the environment variable FINCOMMONS_CONFIG where it is
# set and is otherwise a paths.yaml beside the template.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# What the sector is called on the cover.
sector_name <- c(en = "Construction", de = "Bauwirtschaft")
country_name <- c(en = "Austria", de = "Österreich")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The panel: which issuers the sector is taken to be
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ESEF carries no sector code. A filing states the issuer's legal entity
# identifier and nothing about what it does, and the sector classifications
# the package does hold -- `SECTOR` in fincommons.entitymasterdata -- cover
# financial entities only, a bank, an insurer, a fund. So the panel is a
# stated list, and stating it is the one judgement this factsheet makes that
# the data cannot check.
#
# It is written out with a group per issuer because a construction sector
# read widely is not one population. A contractor turns its balance sheet
# several times a year on advance payments; a developer holds a project for
# years and reports the result when it sells; a materials maker runs a plant
# and carries inventory. Putting them under one median hides exactly what a
# reader of this page is after, so every figure below is shown by group as
# well as for the panel as a whole, and the groups are ordered from the
# building site outwards.
#
# `SHORT` is what the charts and the narrow tables use; `NAME` is not set
# here at all, but read from the table of filings, so that an issuer is
# named as its own report names it.
panel <- tibble::tribble(
  ~LEI,                    ~SHORT,          ~GROUP,                ~NACE,     ~ACTIVITY_EN,                                              ~ACTIVITY_DE,
  "529900TYYSRJH2VJSP60",  "STRABAG",       "contractors",         "F42/F41", "Civil engineering and building construction, Europe-wide", "Hoch- und Tiefbau, europaweit",
  "529900ARBU9SBJFNX419",  "PORR",          "contractors",         "F41/F42", "Building construction and civil engineering, Austria and CEE", "Hoch- und Tiefbau, Österreich und CEE",
  "529900IWRUBPP2VNQB05",  "UBM",           "developers",          "F41.1",   "Development of building projects, residential and office", "Projektentwicklung, Wohnen und Büro",
  "529900VXIFBHO0SW2I31",  "Wienerberger",  "materials",           "C23.32",  "Clay building materials, pipes and surfaces",             "Keramische Baustoffe, Rohre und Flächen",
  "529900HM9YCQHAU2QC84",  "SW Umwelttech", "materials",           "C23.61",  "Precast concrete products for water and infrastructure",  "Betonfertigteile für Wasser und Infrastruktur",
  "5299009A2CSKJBWWKY81",  "Rath",          "materials",           "C23.20",  "Refractory ceramics, sold mainly to industrial plant",    "Feuerfestkeramik, überwiegend für Industrieanlagen",
  "529900WJZJAEI0VBLP60",  "Egger",         "materials",           "C16.21",  "Wood-based panels; a bond issuer, not listed in equity",  "Holzwerkstoffe; Anleihenemittent, nicht börsenotiert",
  "529900IIODYNYAZ2ID26",  "Zumtobel",      "building technology", "C27.40",  "Lighting and lighting components for buildings",          "Leuchten und Lichtkomponenten für Gebäude",
  "52990038OKF8UAD5LA12",  "Frauenthal",    "building technology", "G46.74",  "Wholesale of sanitary and heating technology, and automotive components", "Großhandel mit Sanitär- und Heizungstechnik, und Automotive"
)

# A panel of nine fits in the template and can be read there. A panel of a
# hundred and forty-five -- the construction issuers of twenty-seven
# countries -- does not, and putting it here would bury the code under a
# list. So the panel may instead be read from a csv named in
# FINCOMMONS_PANEL, with the columns of the table above: `LEI`, `SHORT` and
# `GROUP` are required, and `NACE`, `COUNTRY`, `ACTIVITY_EN` and
# `ACTIVITY_DE` are shown where the file has them. The file is a stated list
# exactly as the table above is, and the disclaimer says so of either.
panel_file <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_PANEL", "")
if (nzchar(panel_file)) {
  panel <- utils::read.csv(panel_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                           fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
  required <- c("LEI", "SHORT", "GROUP")
  if (!all(required %in% names(panel))) {
    stop("The panel file ", panel_file, " needs the columns ",
         paste(required, collapse = ", "), "; it has ",
         paste(names(panel), collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
  for (optional in c("NACE", "COUNTRY", "ACTIVITY_EN", "ACTIVITY_DE")) {
    if (!optional %in% names(panel)) panel[[optional]] <- NA_character_
  }
  # A panel file may carry the issuer's name, which is useful to whoever
  # maintains the file and is not what the page prints: the name comes from
  # the table of filings, so that an issuer is named as its own report names
  # it. It is kept under another name rather than dropped, so that a panel
  # whose LEI no longer files can still be named in the gaps.
  if ("NAME" %in% names(panel)) {
    panel$PANEL_NAME <- panel$NAME
    panel$NAME <- NULL
  }
  panel <- tibble::as_tibble(panel)
}
if (anyDuplicated(panel$LEI)) {
  stop("The panel names an issuer twice: ",
       paste(unique(panel$LEI[duplicated(panel$LEI)]), collapse = ", "),
       ". Each issuer belongs to one group.")
}
# The order the groups are shown in, and what they are called. A group the
# panel uses and this vector does not name would be dropped by the factor
# below, so the levels are the named ones first and anything else after
# them, in the order the panel has it.
group_levels <- c("contractors", "developers", "materials",
                  "building technology", "distribution")
group_labels <- c(
  contractors           = "Contractors",
  developers            = "Developers",
  materials             = "Building materials",
  `building technology` = "Building technology",
  distribution          = "Merchants and distribution"
)
group_labels_de <- c(
  contractors           = "Bauunternehmen",
  developers            = "Projektentwickler",
  materials             = "Baustoffe",
  `building technology` = "Gebäudetechnik",
  distribution          = "Baustoffhandel"
)

group_levels <- c(group_levels, setdiff(unique(panel$GROUP), group_levels))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The benchmark
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Which filings the panel is held against. The benchmark is read from the
# combined table of fincommons.financialreport.combined, which carries every
# regime the lake has collected in one shape, so widening the comparison is
# a change to this list and to nothing else: a lake that has collected
# German filings as well gets a European benchmark by putting "DE" beside
# "AT", and one that has run the sec or edinet pipeline gets a cross-regime
# one by naming those sources. NULL means every value the table holds.
#
# A word of warning before that is done, which the combined README sets out
# at length. The measures are not skewed alike between the regimes: a
# `profit_loss` is tagged by nearly every IFRS and Japanese filer and only
# by an American registrant that has non-controlling interests to report,
# so a median of the three put side by side is not a comparison of three
# regimes. Holding `framework` to "IFRS" is the safe way to widen this page
# beyond Europe; naming several frameworks is a decision to be made with
# that section of the README open.
benchmark <- list(
  source    = NULL,   # "esef", "sec", "edinet"; NULL for every one collected
  country   = "AT",   # as the source codes it; NULL for every country
  framework = NULL    # "IFRS", "US-GAAP", "JP-GAAP"; NULL for every one
)

# A bank and an insurer have an equity ratio an eighth of an industrial
# one's, and leaving them in the benchmark would make every issuer of this
# panel look unusually solid for a reason that has nothing to do with
# building. They are therefore named here and shown apart.
#
# Naming them is a stated list for the same reason the panel is: ESEF has no
# sector code. The right source once a lake holds it is `SECTOR` in
# fincommons.entitymasterdata, which the registers of the ECB, EIOPA and
# ESMA fill in and which covers exactly these entities; this list is what a
# lake without that module uses, and it is a list of Austrian filers only.
# A bank and an insurer have an equity ratio an eighth of an industrial
# one's, and leaving them in the benchmark would make every issuer of this
# panel look unusually solid for a reason that has nothing to do with
# building. They are therefore identified and shown apart.
#
# Two things identify them, and the second exists because the first has a
# hole in it.
#
# The first is the sectoral registers, which is where `SECTOR` of
# fincommons.entitymasterdata gets its answer: the ECB's register of
# monetary financial institutions, EIOPA's of insurance undertakings and of
# institutions for occupational retirement provision, and ESMA's list of
# central counterparties. A list of the LEIs on those registers is read from
# the file named in FINCOMMONS_FINANCIAL, one per line.
#
# The hole is twofold and worth stating, because it is the reason the second
# test exists. A register lists the authorised entity, and what files an
# annual financial report is usually the *group* above it: BAWAG P.S.K. is
# on the register and BAWAG Group AG, which files, is not. And the registers
# are European, so a British bank has not been on them since 2020 -- which
# for a lake holding the United Kingdom leaves the largest banks in the
# population unflagged.
#
# The second test closes both, and closes them from the filings themselves:
# a filer whose own primary statements present a line that only a bank or an
# insurer has is one. The concepts are named below rather than guessed at,
# and a filer is flagged by either test.
financial_file <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_FINANCIAL", "")
financial_leis <- if (nzchar(financial_file)) {
  toupper(trimws(readLines(financial_file, warn = FALSE)))
} else character(0)
financial_leis <- financial_leis[nzchar(financial_leis)]

# The lines a bank or an insurer presents and an industrial issuer does not.
# Interest revenue computed with the effective interest method is the
# bank's: IFRS 7 and IAS 1 put it on the face of the statement, and a
# manufacturer that holds a deposit does not present it there. The insurance
# ones are the IFRS 17 lines, which only an insurer has.
financial_concepts <- c(
  "ifrs-full:InterestRevenueCalculatedUsingEffectiveInterestMethod",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceRevenue",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceContractLiabilities",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceServiceResult",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceServiceExpenses"
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The rest of the settings
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The number of financial years shown, counted back from the latest period
# end any issuer of the panel has filed for. One further year is read behind
# them, because a return puts a flow of a year against the balances at its
# start and its end and because the growth rates compare a year with the one
# before it.
n_years <- 5

# Amounts are shown in millions of the target currency.
scale <- 1e6

# The currency every amount is converted into before it is added up. A
# European panel reports in a dozen currencies -- a Swedish contractor in
# krona, a Polish one in zloty, a British one in pounds -- and a sum over
# them is arithmetic on different units unless they are brought to one.
#
# The conversion follows the convention of the supervisory pipelines that
# build on this package, which is worth stating because the column names
# carry it: an amount keeps the figure and the currency the issuer filed,
# and the conversion only ever adds two columns beside it. `<key>_FXRATE`
# is the rate that was applied, which is 1 where the amount was filed in
# the target currency already, and `<key>_DOMESTIC` is the converted
# amount, the filed amount divided by that rate. The name says `DOMESTIC`
# rather than `EUR` so that nothing downstream has to be renamed when the
# target changes.
#
# An amount whose currency the rate table does not quote on its day stays
# unconverted: `_DOMESTIC` is missing, and the sums below pass over it and
# say so in the count beside them. It is never the filed figure carried
# over unconverted, and never a nought.
target_ccy <- "EUR"

# The point size of the text in a chart.
chart_base_size <- 9

# The language of the factsheet.
lang <- "en"

# The month names in the captions come from the system locale rather than
# from the language set above, so the locale for dates is set from lang.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", if (lang == "de") "German" else "C"))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The concepts the panel's own lines are read from
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Only concepts of the IFRS taxonomy. An issuer may tag a line of its
# statements with a concept of its own, and the single-issuer factsheet of
# this module makes room for that one issuer at a time; a page covering nine
# issuers cannot, because an extension concept is each issuer's own to name
# and to rename. A line no issuer of the panel tags under a concept below is
# shown as missing rather than guessed at, and the coverage page at the end
# says for each issuer which of them were found.
#
# A key may carry several concepts, in order of preference, for a line the
# taxonomy offers more than one element for.
concepts <- c(
  assets                           = "ifrs-full:Assets",
  current_assets                   = "ifrs-full:CurrentAssets",
  noncurrent_assets                = "ifrs-full:NoncurrentAssets",
  ppe                              = "ifrs-full:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentIncludingRightofuseAssets",
  ppe                              = "ifrs-full:PropertyPlantAndEquipment",
  goodwill                         = "ifrs-full:Goodwill",
  inventories                      = "ifrs-full:Inventories",
  receivables                      = "ifrs-full:TradeAndOtherCurrentReceivables",
  cash                             = "ifrs-full:CashAndCashEquivalents",

  equity                           = "ifrs-full:Equity",
  equity_owners                    = "ifrs-full:EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent",
  nci                              = "ifrs-full:NoncontrollingInterests",
  liabilities                      = "ifrs-full:Liabilities",
  current_liabilities              = "ifrs-full:CurrentLiabilities",
  noncurrent_liabilities           = "ifrs-full:NoncurrentLiabilities",
  payables                         = "ifrs-full:TradeAndOtherCurrentPayables",
  financial_liabilities_current    = "ifrs-full:OtherCurrentFinancialLiabilities",
  financial_liabilities_noncurrent = "ifrs-full:OtherNoncurrentFinancialLiabilities",
  borrowings_current               = "ifrs-full:ShorttermBorrowings",
  borrowings_noncurrent            = "ifrs-full:LongtermBorrowings",

  revenue                          = "ifrs-full:Revenue",
  revenue                          = "ifrs-full:RevenueFromContractsWithCustomers",
  ebit                             = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossFromOperatingActivities",
  profit_before_tax                = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossBeforeTax",
  income_tax                       = "ifrs-full:IncomeTaxExpenseContinuingOperations",
  profit                           = "ifrs-full:ProfitLoss",
  profit_owners                    = "ifrs-full:ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParent",
  eps                              = "ifrs-full:BasicEarningsLossPerShare",

  operating_cash_flow              = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivities",
  investing_cash_flow              = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInInvestingActivities",
  financing_cash_flow              = "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInFinancingActivities"
)

# The second concept of `revenue` is an approximation and is marked as such
# wherever a figure rests on it: IFRS 15 revenue excludes revenue outside
# that standard which the total may include. It is here because a page that
# shows nothing for an issuer presenting only that line says less than one
# that shows the figure and says what it is. The benchmark, which is read
# from the combined table, does not make that trade: the materialised
# measure names the first concept only, and the README of the combined
# module is where that rule is argued.
approximate_concepts <- c("ifrs-full:RevenueFromContractsWithCustomers")

# You can adapt your corporate design in the sourced R-Skript. It is one file
# for the whole package, in the templates directory at the root of it, so
# that a factsheet of either regime looks like the other and a change to the
# design is made once rather than once per module. A copy beside this
# template wins over it, which is what lets a template taken out of the
# package carry a design of its own.
library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)

# Translate a label: `tr("Revenue", "Umsatzerlöse")`.
tr <- function(en, de) if (lang == "de") de else en

# The label of a financial year. A year that ends on 31 December is named by
# its calendar year, and any other by the two it spans: Zumtobel's year to
# 30 April 2025 is 2024/25.
fy_label <- function(date) {
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ifelse(format(date, "%m-%d") == "12-31", as.character(y),
         paste0(y - 1, "/", sprintf("%02d", y %% 100)))
}

big_mark <- tr(",", ".")
decimal_mark <- tr(".", ",")

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = big_mark,
                 decimal.mark = decimal_mark))
}

fmt_signed <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""),
                formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = big_mark,
                        decimal.mark = decimal_mark)))
}

# A caption wider than the figure is clipped rather than wrapped, so it is
# broken into lines once here.
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

# Escape what typst reads as its own syntax, for the text that goes into the
# raw blocks of the cover and of the running head.
typst_string <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}

group_label <- function(key) {
  labels <- if (lang == "de") group_labels_de else group_labels
  out <- unname(labels[key])
  ifelse(is.na(out), key, out)
}
```

```{r lake}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)

silver_of <- function(section) {
  entry <- yaml_paths[[section]][["silver"]]
  # The Silver layer may name a schema in a catalogue rather than a
  # directory, with the directory the tables are written to beside it. R
  # reads files, so it takes the directory.
  if (is.list(entry)) entry <- entry[["path"]]
  entry
}

# arrow reads every parquet file under a directory. A Delta table keeps the
# files it has replaced until it is vacuumed, and both of these tables are
# rebuilt in full, so a Delta table read this way would count a fact once
# for every time it was written. The factsheet refuses one rather than show
# those sums.
refuse_delta <- function(path, table, module) {
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the ", module, " module is a Delta table, ",
         "which this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as ",
         "parquet, or read the table through Spark.")
  }
}

path_esef <- silver_of("esef")
if (is.null(path_esef)) {
  stop("The configuration file ", config_path, " names no esef section. ",
       "This factsheet reads the panel's own lines from the esef tables.")
}
for (table in c("filings", "facts")) refuse_delta(path_esef, table, "esef")

filings_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_esef, "filings")) %>%
  filter(LEI %in% panel$LEI) %>%
  collect()

missing_issuers <- setdiff(panel$LEI, filings_all$LEI)
if (length(missing_issuers) == nrow(panel)) {
  stop("The table of filings lists no filing of any issuer of the panel. ",
       "The table lists every country whether its reports were collected or ",
       "not, so either the identifiers are wrong or the lake is empty.")
}

# One filing per issuer and financial year. A report filed in two languages,
# or filed again with corrections, is a filing of its own with facts of its
# own, and the figures of the year are taken from one of them: the one in
# the language of the factsheet, then the one with fewer validation errors,
# then the one the repository processed last. A filing without a JSONURL has
# no facts and is never chosen while another one is there.
filings <- filings_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(JSONURL)) %>%
  arrange(LEI, PERIODEND,
          coalesce(LANG, "") != lang,
          coalesce(ERRORS, 0L),
          desc(PROCESSED)) %>%
  group_by(LEI, PERIODEND) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

if (nrow(filings) == 0) {
  stop("No filing of any issuer of the panel has facts in the Silver layer. ",
       "Run the esef pipeline for the country of the panel first.")
}

# The years the page shows: the last `n_years` period ends of the panel,
# plus one behind them for the growth rates and the average balances. An
# issuer whose financial year does not end in December is counted into the
# year its period end falls in, and labelled as the two years it spans.
period_year <- function(date) {
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ifelse(as.integer(format(date, "%m")) <= 6L, y - 1L, y)
}

filings <- filings %>% mutate(FY = period_year(PERIODEND))
years_shown <- sort(unique(filings$FY)) %>% tail(n_years)
years_read <- sort(unique(filings$FY)) %>% tail(n_years + 1)
filings <- filings %>% filter(FY %in% years_read)

facts <- open_dataset(file.path(path_esef, "facts")) %>%
  filter(FILING %in% filings$FILING) %>%
  collect()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The combined table, which the benchmark is read from
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The benchmark is a question about a population rather than about named
# facts, and the combined table is where this package answers one: it
# carries every regime the lake has collected in the same columns, and the
# column `MEASURE` names what a fact is wherever the catalogue of measures
# has agreed that the frameworks mean the same figure by it.
#
# What that column does not carry is as important as what it does. Only the
# first concept of each framework is named, so a filing stating revenue only
# as IFRS 15 revenue carries no measure and is absent from the benchmark;
# and `profit_loss` is the total including the non-controlling interests, so
# an American registrant tagging only `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss` is absent too.
# The counts beside every benchmark figure on this page are therefore counts
# of filings that stated and named the figure, never of the population.
path_combined <- silver_of("financialreport")
has_combined <- !is.null(path_combined) &&
  dir.exists(file.path(path_combined, "fact"))

if (has_combined) {
  for (table in c("fact", "filing")) {
    refuse_delta(path_combined, table, "financialreport")
  }

  bench_filings <- open_dataset(file.path(path_combined, "filing")) %>%
    collect()
  if (!is.null(benchmark$source)) {
    bench_filings <- bench_filings %>% filter(SOURCE %in% benchmark$source)
  }
  if (!is.null(benchmark$country)) {
    bench_filings <- bench_filings %>% filter(COUNTRY %in% benchmark$country)
  }
  if (!is.null(benchmark$framework)) {
    bench_filings <- bench_filings %>% filter(FRAMEWORK %in% benchmark$framework)
  }

  bench_facts <- open_dataset(file.path(path_combined, "fact")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(MEASURE), FILING %in% bench_filings$FILING) %>%
    collect()

  # The second test for a bank or an insurer: a filer whose own primary
  # statements carry a line only a financial undertaking has. It is a
  # separate read because these concepts carry no measure, which is what
  # `bench_facts` is filtered on.
  financial_by_statement <- open_dataset(file.path(path_combined, "fact")) %>%
    filter(CONCEPT %in% financial_concepts,
           FILING %in% bench_filings$FILING) %>%
    select(LEI) %>%
    collect() %>%
    distinct() %>%
    pull("LEI")
  financial_by_statement <- financial_by_statement[!is.na(financial_by_statement)]
} else {
  bench_filings <- filings[0, ]
  bench_facts <- NULL
  financial_by_statement <- character(0)
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The exchange rates
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# One row per calendar day and quoted currency, the table of
# fincommons.exchangerate, which carries the last rate quoted on or before a
# day for at most a week after that quote and marks a carried rate as
# `IMPUTED`. It is read only where the panel needs it, so a lake holding one
# currency needs no exchangerate section at all.
path_fx <- silver_of("exchangerate")
fx <- NULL
if (!is.null(path_fx) && dir.exists(file.path(path_fx, "exchangerate"))) {
  refuse_delta(path_fx, "exchangerate", "exchangerate")
  fx <- open_dataset(file.path(path_fx, "exchangerate")) %>%
    filter(BASE == target_ccy) %>%
    select(REFDATE, QUOTE, VALUE, IMPUTED) %>%
    collect() %>%
    mutate(REFDATE = as.Date(REFDATE))
  if (nrow(fx) == 0) fx <- NULL
}
```

```{r figures}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The panel's own figures, one row per issuer and financial year
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The figures of a year are the totals the year's own filing reports for the
# year: no dimensions, a period that ends on the period end of the filing,
# and, for a flow, a period that begins a year before it. The comparative
# figures of the previous year that every filing carries as well are left
# aside, so that a restated figure does not stand beside the one first
# reported without saying so.
annual <- facts %>%
  filter(is.na(DIMENSIONS), !is.na(VALUE), PRDEND == PERIODEND,
         is.na(PRDSTART) | PRDSTART >= PERIODEND - 366) %>%
  left_join(filings %>% select(FILING, FY), by = "FILING") %>%
  distinct(LEI, FY, PERIODEND, PRDSTART, CONCEPT, UNIT, VALUE)

lookup <- tibble(key = names(concepts), CONCEPT = unname(concepts),
                 preference = seq_along(concepts))

tagged <- annual %>%
  inner_join(lookup, by = "CONCEPT", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(LEI, FY, key) %>%
  slice_min(preference, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

wide <- tagged %>%
  select(LEI, FY, PERIODEND, key, VALUE) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "key", values_from = "VALUE") %>%
  arrange(LEI, FY)
for (key in setdiff(unique(names(concepts)), names(wide))) {
  wide[[key]] <- NA_real_
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The currency of each issuer, and the conversion into the target
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The currency a filing reports in, taken from the unit of its total assets.
# It is read per issuer and year rather than once for the panel, because an
# issuer may redenominate -- a Croatian one did, on the euro changeover of
# 2023 -- and because a European panel has a dozen of them at once.
reported_ccy <- tagged %>%
  filter(key == "assets", !is.na(UNIT)) %>%
  transmute(LEI, FY, CCY = sub("^iso4217:", "", UNIT)) %>%
  distinct(LEI, FY, .keep_all = TRUE)

wide <- wide %>% left_join(reported_ccy, by = c("LEI", "FY"))

currencies <- sort(unique(wide$CCY[!is.na(wide$CCY)]))
needs_fx <- any(currencies != target_ccy)
amount_label <- tr(paste0(target_ccy, " million"), paste0("Mio. ", target_ccy))

# The rate table is required only where something has to be converted, and
# where it is required it has to carry rates: a table with none would
# convert every amount to a missing value and the page would read as a
# sector that reported nothing rather than as a page that could not be
# built. This is the check the EMIR and SFTR pipelines make for the same
# reason, and it is made here before anything is converted.
if (needs_fx && is.null(fx)) {
  stop("The issuers of the panel report in more than one currency (",
       paste(currencies, collapse = ", "), ") and the lake holds no ",
       "exchange rate table quoted against ", target_ccy, ". Build it with ",
       "fincommons.exchangerate.update_exchangerate and name its layers in ",
       "the exchangerate section of ", config_path, ", or hold the panel to ",
       "one currency.")
}

# The first day of the financial year, from the flows of the filing itself
# rather than counted back from the period end, so that a year that is not
# twelve months long is averaged over the months it has.
period_start <- annual %>%
  filter(!is.na(PRDSTART)) %>%
  group_by(LEI, FY) %>%
  summarise(PRDSTART = min(PRDSTART), .groups = "drop")

wide <- wide %>%
  left_join(period_start, by = c("LEI", "FY")) %>%
  mutate(PRDSTART = coalesce(PRDSTART, PERIODEND - 364))

# Two rates per filing, because IAS 21 translates the two kinds of figure
# differently and a factsheet that adds up translated amounts should do what
# the standard does. A balance is translated at the closing rate of the
# reporting date; income and expense at the average rate of the period,
# which is taken here over the daily rates of the financial year. A rate
# that is not quoted on the closing date itself does not arise, the table
# carrying one row per calendar day, but a currency the table does not quote
# at all leaves both rates missing.
rate_on <- function(ccy, day) {
  if (is.na(ccy) || is.na(day)) return(NA_real_)
  if (ccy == target_ccy) return(1)
  v <- fx$VALUE[fx$QUOTE == ccy & fx$REFDATE == day]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v[1]
}
rate_over <- function(ccy, from, to) {
  if (is.na(ccy) || is.na(from) || is.na(to)) return(NA_real_)
  if (ccy == target_ccy) return(1)
  v <- fx$VALUE[fx$QUOTE == ccy & fx$REFDATE >= from & fx$REFDATE <= to]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else mean(v)
}

wide$FXRATE_CLOSING <- if (needs_fx) {
  mapply(rate_on, wide$CCY, wide$PERIODEND)
} else rep(1, nrow(wide))
wide$FXRATE_AVERAGE <- if (needs_fx) {
  mapply(rate_over, wide$CCY, wide$PRDSTART, wide$PERIODEND)
} else rep(1, nrow(wide))

# The amounts, and which of the two rates each is translated at. A key that
# is neither is not an amount -- a ratio, a per-share figure, a date -- and
# is never converted.
instant_keys <- c("assets", "current_assets", "noncurrent_assets", "ppe",
                  "goodwill", "inventories", "receivables", "cash",
                  "equity", "equity_owners", "nci", "liabilities",
                  "current_liabilities", "noncurrent_liabilities", "payables",
                  "financial_liabilities_current",
                  "financial_liabilities_noncurrent",
                  "borrowings_current", "borrowings_noncurrent")
flow_keys <- c("revenue", "ebit", "profit_before_tax", "income_tax", "profit",
               "profit_owners", "operating_cash_flow", "investing_cash_flow",
               "financing_cash_flow")

# The derived lines. Nothing here is a figure an issuer stated: each is
# arithmetic on figures it did state, and a line resting on a figure the
# issuer did not tag stays missing rather than taking a nought for it.
#
# Net debt is the borrowings and the other financial liabilities, current
# and non-current, less cash. No issuer tags a net debt of its own under a
# concept of the taxonomy, and the figure a report states in its management
# report is usually defined more widely, so the one here is not the one the
# issuer reports.
#
# EBITDA is not derived. Depreciation and amortisation are not a line of the
# primary statements under a concept of the IFRS taxonomy, so every
# indicator that would rest on EBITDA is shown against EBIT or against the
# operating cash flow instead.
wide <- wide %>%
  left_join(panel, by = "LEI") %>%
  group_by(LEI) %>%
  arrange(FY, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    year = fy_label(PERIODEND),
    liabilities = coalesce(liabilities, assets - equity),
    financial_liabilities =
      coalesce(financial_liabilities_noncurrent, borrowings_noncurrent, 0) +
      coalesce(financial_liabilities_current, borrowings_current, 0),
    net_debt = ifelse(
      is.na(financial_liabilities_noncurrent) & is.na(borrowings_noncurrent) &
        is.na(financial_liabilities_current) & is.na(borrowings_current),
      NA_real_, financial_liabilities - coalesce(cash, 0)),
    working_capital = inventories + receivables - payables,
    equity_ratio = 100 * equity / assets,
    ebit_margin = 100 * ebit / revenue,
    net_margin = 100 * profit / revenue,
    assets_turnover = revenue / assets,
    current_ratio = current_assets / current_liabilities,
    cash_conversion = 100 * operating_cash_flow / ebit,
    equity_avg = (equity + lag(equity)) / 2,
    assets_avg = (assets + lag(assets)) / 2,
    roe = 100 * profit / equity_avg,
    roa = 100 * profit / assets_avg,
    revenue_growth = 100 * (revenue / lag(revenue) - 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(GROUP = factor(GROUP, levels = group_levels))

# The conversion runs here, once the derived amounts exist, so that a net
# debt or a working capital is translated like the lines it was built from
# rather than left in the issuer's own currency. The derived keys are
# translated at the closing rate, every one of them being a balance.
instant_keys <- c(instant_keys, "financial_liabilities", "net_debt",
                  "working_capital", "equity_avg", "assets_avg")

for (key in c(instant_keys, flow_keys)) {
  if (!key %in% names(wide)) next
  rate <- if (key %in% instant_keys) wide$FXRATE_CLOSING else wide$FXRATE_AVERAGE
  wide[[paste0(key, "_FXRATE")]] <- rate
  wide[[paste0(key, "_DOMESTIC")]] <- wide[[key]] / rate
}

# An amount is shown and added up in the target currency; a ratio is not
# converted at all. A margin, an equity ratio or a return is a quotient of
# two amounts of one filing in one currency, so the currency cancels, and
# computing it from the filed figures rather than from the converted ones
# keeps it answerable for an issuer whose currency the rate table does not
# quote. `dom` is how the rest of this template asks for an amount.
dom <- function(data, key) data[[paste0(key, "_DOMESTIC")]]

# The issuer-years whose amounts could not be converted, which the page
# names rather than passing over. A missing rate leaves a missing amount and
# the issuer drops out of a sum; it is never the filed figure counted as
# though it were already in the target currency.
unconverted <- wide %>%
  filter(FY %in% years_shown, !is.na(assets), is.na(assets_DOMESTIC)) %>%
  select(LEI, FY, CCY)

# Which lines rest on a concept the catalogue calls an approximation, so the
# tables can mark them.
approximate <- tagged %>%
  filter(CONCEPT %in% approximate_concepts) %>%
  distinct(LEI, FY, key)

shown <- wide %>% filter(FY %in% years_shown)
latest_year <- max(years_shown)
latest <- shown %>% filter(FY == latest_year)

# An issuer that has stopped filing has no row in the latest year, and the
# page says so rather than dropping it without a word.
absent_latest <- panel %>%
  filter(!LEI %in% latest$LEI) %>%
  left_join(wide %>% group_by(LEI) %>%
              summarise(last_year = max(FY), .groups = "drop"), by = "LEI")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The sector totals
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A total is the sum of the issuers that stated the figure in that year, and
# the count beside it says how many those were. A sum over a changing number
# of issuers is not a time series of the sector, which is why the count is
# never dropped and why the growth of the sector further down is computed
# over the issuers present in both years rather than over the totals.
# The totals are grouped by the financial year rather than by its label:
# Zumtobel's year to 30 April 2026 and STRABAG's to 31 December 2025 are the
# same financial year of the sector, and `period_year` is what puts them
# there. Each issuer keeps its own label in the tables that show it alone.
totals <- shown %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarise(across(ends_with("_DOMESTIC"),
                   list(sum = ~sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        n = ~sum(!is.na(.x)))),
            issuers = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename_with(~sub("_DOMESTIC_", "_", .x)) %>%
  arrange(FY)

# Growth of the sector, over the issuers that filed in both years.
like_for_like <- shown %>%
  transmute(LEI, FY, revenue = revenue_DOMESTIC) %>%
  arrange(LEI, FY) %>%
  group_by(LEI) %>%
  mutate(prev = lag(revenue), prev_fy = lag(FY)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(revenue), !is.na(prev), FY == prev_fy + 1) %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarise(revenue = sum(revenue), prev = sum(prev), issuers = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(growth = 100 * (revenue / prev - 1))

# The same sums, group by group. A group is shown with the number of issuers
# behind it because three of the four have fewer than four, and a median of
# two is a midpoint rather than a benchmark. They are here so that a reader
# can see which part of the sector a movement in the total came from: the
# groups do not move together, and that is the whole reason the panel
# carries a group per issuer rather than one label for all of them.
by_group <- shown %>%
  group_by(GROUP, FY) %>%
  summarise(across(c(revenue_DOMESTIC, ebit_DOMESTIC, profit_DOMESTIC,
                     assets_DOMESTIC, equity_DOMESTIC),
                   ~sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            issuers = n_distinct(LEI), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename_with(~sub("_DOMESTIC$", "", .x)) %>%
  mutate(ebit_margin = 100 * ebit / revenue,
         equity_ratio = 100 * equity / assets) %>%
  arrange(GROUP, FY)
```

```{r benchmark}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The benchmark, from the materialised measures of the combined table
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# One value per filing and measure, for the year the filing reports on. A
# fact under a dimension is a part of the entity rather than the entity, and
# is left out; `BASIS_MEMBERS` of the combined module is the one exception
# the Python side makes, for a Japanese filing that states its parent
# company's accounts under a member, and it does not arise in a table of
# ESEF filings.
measures_wanted <- c("revenue", "assets", "liabilities", "equity",
                     "profit_loss", "cash_and_equivalents")

if (has_combined) {
  bench_values <- bench_facts %>%
    filter(is.na(DIMENSIONS), !is.na(VALUE), MEASURE %in% measures_wanted,
           PRDEND == PERIODEND) %>%
    distinct(SOURCE, FILING, LEI, PERIODEND, PERIODYEAR, MEASURE, VALUE) %>%
    group_by(FILING, PERIODEND, MEASURE) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "MEASURE", values_from = "VALUE") %>%
    mutate(FY = period_year(PERIODEND))
  for (key in setdiff(measures_wanted, names(bench_values))) {
    bench_values[[key]] <- NA_real_
  }

  # One filing per issuer and year, the same rule as for the panel: the
  # filing that carries the most of the measures wins, and the identifier
  # breaks a tie so that the choice is the same on every run.
  bench_values <- bench_values %>%
    mutate(filled = rowSums(!is.na(across(all_of(measures_wanted))))) %>%
    arrange(LEI, FY, desc(filled), FILING) %>%
    group_by(LEI, FY) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      financial = LEI %in% financial_leis | LEI %in% financial_by_statement,
      in_panel  = LEI %in% panel$LEI,
      equity_ratio = 100 * equity / assets,
      net_margin   = 100 * profit_loss / revenue,
      roe          = 100 * profit_loss / equity,
      roa          = 100 * profit_loss / assets,
      cash_ratio   = 100 * cash_and_equivalents / assets
    )

  # The population the panel is held against: everything the scope above
  # names, less the banks and insurers, and less the panel itself, so that
  # the panel is not being compared with a median it is a part of.
  market <- bench_values %>% filter(!financial, !in_panel)
} else {
  bench_values <- NULL
  market <- NULL
}

bench_ratios <- c("equity_ratio", "net_margin", "roe", "roa")
bench_ratio_labels <- c(
  equity_ratio = tr("Equity ratio, %", "Eigenkapitalquote, %"),
  net_margin   = tr("Net margin, %", "Nettomarge, %"),
  roe          = tr("Return on equity, %", "Eigenkapitalrendite, %"),
  roa          = tr("Return on assets, %", "Gesamtkapitalrendite, %")
)

# The quartiles of the population in the latest year, and of the panel
# beside them. A ratio is only read where both of its figures were stated,
# and `n` says how many filings that was.
quartiles <- function(data, key) {
  v <- data[[key]]
  v <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (length(v) == 0) {
    return(tibble(q1 = NA_real_, median = NA_real_, q3 = NA_real_, n = 0L))
  }
  tibble(q1 = unname(quantile(v, .25)), median = median(v),
         q3 = unname(quantile(v, .75)), n = length(v))
}

bench_table <- NULL
if (has_combined && nrow(market) > 0) {
  bench_table <- lapply(bench_ratios, function(key) {
    bind_rows(
      quartiles(bench_values %>% filter(in_panel, FY == latest_year), key) %>%
        mutate(population = tr("The panel", "Das Panel")),
      quartiles(market %>% filter(FY == latest_year), key) %>%
        mutate(population = tr("Other filers, excluding banks and insurers",
                               "Übrige Emittenten, ohne Banken und Versicherer")),
      quartiles(bench_values %>% filter(financial, FY == latest_year), key) %>%
        mutate(population = tr("Banks and insurers", "Banken und Versicherer"))
    ) %>% mutate(ratio = key)
  }) %>% bind_rows()
}

# The median of the population, year by year, for the charts that put the
# panel against a band.
market_band <- NULL
if (has_combined && nrow(market) > 0) {
  market_band <- lapply(bench_ratios, function(key) {
    market %>%
      filter(FY %in% years_shown) %>%
      group_by(FY) %>%
      group_modify(~quartiles(.x, key)) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(ratio = key)
  }) %>% bind_rows()
}
```

```{r charts}
                     expand = c(.04, 0), ...)
}
```

### `r tr("How the figures are put together", "Wie die Zahlen zustande kommen")`

`r tr(paste0("Every figure on this page is a fact an issuer tagged in its own annual financial report, read from the ESEF tables of fincommons. A report is filed in Inline XBRL with the officially appointed mechanism of its member state and collected by filings.xbrl.org, which is where the pipeline reads it from. Nothing here is estimated, interpolated or converted: a line an issuer did not tag is shown as a dash, and a ratio whose two figures were not both stated is not computed."), paste0("Jede Zahl auf dieser Seite ist ein Fakt, den ein Emittent in seinem eigenen Jahresfinanzbericht ausgezeichnet hat, gelesen aus den ESEF-Tabellen von fincommons. Ein Bericht wird in Inline XBRL beim Speichersystem seines Mitgliedstaats eingereicht und von filings.xbrl.org gesammelt, von wo die Pipeline ihn liest. Nichts ist geschätzt, interpoliert oder umgerechnet: eine Zeile, die ein Emittent nicht ausgezeichnet hat, steht als Strich, und eine Kennzahl, deren beide Größen nicht beide angegeben wurden, wird nicht berechnet."))`

`r tr("The sector is a stated list. ESEF carries no sector code, so which issuer belongs to a construction sector is a judgement, and it is made in the panel below rather than anywhere in the data. Each issuer is shown with the group it was put in, so that a reader who would draw the boundary elsewhere can see what moving it would do.", "Der Sektor ist eine gesetzte Liste. ESEF enthält keinen Branchencode, daher ist die Zuordnung eines Emittenten zur Bauwirtschaft eine Setzung, und sie wird im Panel unten getroffen und nirgends in den Daten. Jeder Emittent wird mit seiner Gruppe gezeigt, damit erkennbar bleibt, was eine andere Abgrenzung ändern würde.")`

### `r tr("Amounts in one currency", "Beträge in einer Währung")`

```{r currency-note, results = "asis"}
if (!needs_fx) {
  cat(tr(paste0("Every issuer of the panel reports in ", target_ccy,
                ", so nothing is converted."),
         paste0("Alle Emittenten des Panels berichten in ", target_ccy,
                "; es wird nichts umgerechnet.")), "\n")
} else {
  cat(tr(
    paste0("The issuers of this panel report in ", length(currencies),
           " currencies (", paste(currencies, collapse = ", "), "). Every ",
           "amount on these pages is therefore shown converted into ",
           target_ccy, ", at the reference rates of ",
           "fincommons.exchangerate. The figure the issuer filed and the ",
           "currency it filed it in are kept untouched beside it; the ",
           "conversion only adds the rate that was applied and the ",
           "converted amount. A balance is converted at the closing rate of ",
           "the reporting date and an income or expense at the average rate ",
           "of the financial year, which is what IAS 21 does and what makes ",
           "a translated margin mean what it says.\n\n",
           "A ratio is not converted at all. A margin, an equity ratio and ",
           "a return are each a quotient of two amounts of one filing in ",
           "one currency, so the currency cancels, and they are computed ",
           "from the figures as filed. That is why an issuer whose currency ",
           "the rate table does not reach can still stand in the ",
           "benchmark while its amounts are missing from the sums."),
    paste0("Die Emittenten dieses Panels berichten in ", length(currencies),
           " Währungen (", paste(currencies, collapse = ", "), "). Jeder ",
           "Betrag auf diesen Seiten wird daher in ", target_ccy,
           " umgerechnet gezeigt, zu den Referenzkursen von ",
           "fincommons.exchangerate. Der vom Emittenten eingereichte Wert ",
           "und dessen Währung bleiben unangetastet daneben stehen; die ",
           "Umrechnung fügt nur den angewandten Kurs und den umgerechneten ",
           "Betrag hinzu. Ein Bestand wird zum Stichtagskurs umgerechnet, ",
           "ein Ertrag oder Aufwand zum Durchschnittskurs des ",
           "Geschäftsjahres -- so wie es IAS 21 vorsieht.\n\n",
           "Eine Kennzahl wird gar nicht umgerechnet. Marge, ",
           "Eigenkapitalquote und Rendite sind Quotienten zweier Größen ",
           "eines Berichts in einer Währung; die Währung kürzt sich heraus, ",
           "und sie werden aus den eingereichten Werten berechnet.")),
      "\n")
}
if (nrow(unconverted) > 0) {
  missing <- unconverted %>%
    left_join(panel %>% select(LEI, SHORT), by = "LEI") %>%
    mutate(txt = paste0(SHORT, " ", FY, " (", CCY, ")"))
  cat("\n\n", tr(
    paste0("The rate table does not quote ", nrow(unconverted),
           " of the issuer-years shown: ",
           paste(missing$txt, collapse = ", "),
           ". Those amounts are missing rather than carried over ",
           "unconverted, and the counts beside the sums are smaller by that ",
           "many."),
    paste0("Für ", nrow(unconverted), " der gezeigten Emittentenjahre ",
           "liefert die Kurstabelle keinen Kurs: ",
           paste(missing$txt, collapse = ", "),
           ". Diese Beträge fehlen, statt unumgerechnet übernommen zu ",
           "werden; die Anzahl neben den Summen ist entsprechend kleiner.")),
      "\n")
}
```

## `r tr("The panel", "Das Panel")`

```{r panel-table}
temp <- panel %>%
  left_join(filings %>%
              arrange(LEI, desc(PERIODEND)) %>%
              group_by(LEI) %>%
              summarise(NAME = first(NAME),
                        first_year = fy_label(min(PERIODEND)),
                        last_year = fy_label(max(PERIODEND)),
                        filings = n(), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "LEI") %>%
  mutate(GROUP = factor(GROUP, levels = group_levels)) %>%
  arrange(GROUP, SHORT) %>%
  transmute(
    !!tr("Issuer", "Emittent") := coalesce(NAME, SHORT),
    !!tr("Group", "Gruppe") := group_label(as.character(GROUP)),
    !!tr("NACE", "NACE") := NACE,
    !!tr("Country", "Land") := COUNTRY,
    !!tr("What it does", "Tätigkeit") :=
      if (lang == "de") ACTIVITY_DE else ACTIVITY_EN,
    !!tr("Years filed", "Jahre") := paste0(first_year, "–", last_year),
    !!tr("Filings", "Berichte") := filings)

# A column every row leaves empty is dropped rather than printed as a
# column of dashes: a panel file that names no activity should not cost the
# table a column.
temp <- temp[, vapply(temp, function(x) any(!is.na(x) & x != ""), logical(1)),
             drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(temp, align = paste(rep("l", ncol(temp)), collapse = ""))
```

### `r tr("Each issuer against its own first year", "Jeder Emittent gegen sein eigenes erstes Jahr")`

```{r revenue-index, fig.height = 2.8}
# The index is taken on the converted revenue rather than on the filed one,
# because an issuer that redenominated -- as the Croatian ones did on the
# euro changeover of 2023 -- has a filed series in two units, and an index
# over that would be a step rather than a growth rate.
base <- shown %>%
  filter(!is.na(revenue_DOMESTIC)) %>%
  group_by(LEI) %>%
  arrange(FY, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(index = 100 * revenue_DOMESTIC / first(revenue_DOMESTIC)) %>%
  ungroup()

g <- ggplot(base, aes(x = FY, y = index, colour = GROUP, group = SHORT)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = design_colours()["grid"]) +
  geom_line(linewidth = linewidth_corporate_design) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_x_years() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colours, labels = group_label,
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = tr("First year = 100", "Erstes Jahr = 100"),
       caption = source_caption) +
  theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size)
g
```

```{r coverage-table}
wanted <- c("revenue", "ebit", "profit", "assets", "equity",
            "operating_cash_flow", "net_debt")
wanted_labels <- c(
  revenue             = tr("Revenue", "Umsatz"),
  ebit                = tr("EBIT", "EBIT"),
  profit              = tr("Result", "Ergebnis"),
  assets              = tr("Assets", "Bilanzsumme"),
  equity              = tr("Equity", "Eigenkapital"),
  operating_cash_flow = tr("Operating cash flow", "Operativer Cashflow"),
  net_debt            = tr("Net debt", "Nettofinanzschulden"))

temp <- shown %>%
  group_by(SHORT, GROUP) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(wanted), ~sum(!is.na(.x))),
            years = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(GROUP, SHORT)

out <- temp %>%
  transmute(!!tr("Issuer", "Emittent") := SHORT,
            !!tr("Years", "Jahre") := years)
for (key in wanted) {
  out[[unname(wanted_labels[key])]] <- temp[[key]]
}

             caption = tr(
               paste0("In how many of the ", length(years_shown),
                      " years shown each line was tagged. A nought is a line ",
                      "the issuer never tagged under a concept of the IFRS ",
                      "taxonomy; it may still stand in the report under a ",
                      "concept of the issuer's own, which this page does not ",
                      "read."),

                      " gezeigten Jahre die Zeile ausgezeichnet wurde. Eine ",
                      "Null ist eine Zeile, die der Emittent nie unter einem ",
```

```{r disclaimer, results='asis'}
# The last word on the last page, the counterpart of the one the
# single-issuer factsheet carries. It says one thing more than that one
# does, and it is the thing this template adds: the panel is a judgement,
# not a classification, and a reader who takes the medians of these pages
# for the medians of a sector is being told here that they are not.
cat(tr(
  paste0(
    "**An example, not a service.** This document is produced by a template ",
    "of the open-source project fincommons, which is published to show what ",
    "the annual financial reports filed in the European Single Electronic ",
    "Format contain and how they can be read. The issuers are examples, ",
    "chosen because their filings are public; the figures illustrate what ",
    "the tagged facts of those filings yield. The document is not a ",
    "financial product, not a research publication, not an investor ",
    "communication and not a service rendered to anyone. It is produced ",
    "automatically, no one reviews it before it is produced, and whoever ",
    "renders or passes it on is responsible for what they do with it.\n\n",
    "**The panel is a judgement, not a classification.** No sector code is ",
    "filed with an ESEF report, and no classification was applied to ",
    "arrive at these issuers. Whoever set the panel decided which issuers ",
    "stand for the sector and which group each belongs to, and a different ",
    "panel would give different totals, different medians and a different ",
    "picture. The panel is printed in full at the front of this document ",
    "for that reason. Nothing here is a statement about a sector of the ",
    "economy, about a national accounts aggregate or about any population ",
    "wider than the issuers named: the listed issuers of a country are a ",
    "small and unrepresentative part of its industry, and the large private ",
    "companies of this one are absent because they file no report of this ",
    "kind. The same applies to the list of banks and insurers the benchmark ",
    "is shown without, which is a stated list as well.\n\n",
    "**No warranty as to correctness.** The template and this document are ",
    "provided as is and without warranty of any kind, express or implied, ",
    "including as to accuracy, absence of errors, merchantability or ",
    "fitness for any purpose. No guarantee is given that a figure on these ",
    "pages is correct. A figure can be wrong because the report it was read ",
    "from tagged it wrongly, because a concept of the taxonomy was used for ",
    "something other than what is assumed here, because the repository's ",
    "copy of a filing is faulty, or because a figure derived on these pages ",
    "is derived differently from the way an issuer derives the figure it ",
    "calls by that name. The audited financial statements of each issuer ",
    "are the authoritative source and prevail wherever they differ from ",
    "anything shown here. A figure is shown as it was reported for its own ",
    "year and is not restated.\n\n",
    "**A total is a sum of what was stated.** Every sum on these pages runs ",
    "over the issuers that tagged the figure in that year and whose amount ",
    "could be converted, and the count beside it says how many those were. ",
    "A sum is not a sector aggregate, a count of issuers carrying a figure ",
    "is not a population, and an absent figure is never read as a nought. ",
    "Where the issuers report in more than one currency the amounts are ",
    "converted at published reference rates, a balance at the closing rate ",
    "of its reporting date and an income or expense at the average rate of ",
    "its period; a converted amount is an arithmetic translation and not the ",
    "figure the issuer reported, which stands unchanged in its own report. ",

    "ratio, and a ratio is computed before any conversion.\n\n",
    "**No warranty as to completeness.** These pages hold what the reports ",
    "tag and nothing beyond it. A line of the statements an issuer did not ",
    "tag, the notes, the management report, the auditor's report, the ",
    "events after the reporting period and every non-financial disclosure ",

    "authorised, sponsored, commissioned or reviewed by any issuer named ",
    "here, by XBRL International, by the officially appointed mechanism of ",
```
